text:
olivia: FYI I posted an RFC draft for a Tenant-Shared Sidecar (TSS) pattern — https://r.rw/rfc/tss-draft. TL;DR: instead of duplicating tenant auth/flags/quota logic across services we run a lightweight sidecar per node-pool that serves those concerns over a local socket. Advantages: single rollout, consistent telemetry, easier fixes. Tradeoffs: new service + ops surface, careful isolation design needed. Asking for quick feedback on viability and migration plan.

samir: quick q — why sidecar vs shared library? duplication is annoying but adding another service sounds heavier.

olivia: good question. library approach keeps code local but we've tripped over inconsistent bugfixes 3x this quarter (flags mismatch, quota off by tenant). Sidecar centralizes the logic so we can fix once and roll out. We expect <1ms local socket calls for cache hits; remote lookups are async/fallback. Also allows independent scaling per workload.

cheng: security concern — will the sidecar hold tenant secrets or do crypto operations? what's the trust boundary?

olivia: sidecar will NOT store raw customer secrets or PII. It serves metadata, flags, quotas, and issues short-lived signed assertions for the data plane. KMS/HSM operations remain in control plane for key material; sidecar will cache signed assertions (TTL short). We'll define strict PDP rules in the RFC.

maya: migration plan idea: 1) sidecar read-only flags -> 2) caching layer and monitoring -> 3) quota check proxying -> 4) enforce mode. That minimizes blast radius.

samir: what about perf? we can't add 5-10ms to hotpath calls. do we have numbers?

olivia: did a 2-node spike: local unix domain socket + in-proc cache gives ~0.6ms median for flags reads, 95th ~1.4ms. Remote cold lookups were 8-12ms. Plan is to keep path hot by local cache; fallback async refresh. If a route is sensitive to +latency we can annotate it to skip the RPC and use cached assertions. Bench notes in RFC.

cheng: API surface? can you paste a sketch?

olivia: sure — rough HTTP/JSON proto we discussed: 

```
GET /v1/tenant/{tid}/flags -> {"flags": {...}, "ttl_ms": 3000}
POST /v1/tenant/{tid}/check_quota {"route":"/generate","units":1} -> {"allowed":true,"remaining":123}
POST /v1/tenant/{tid}/assert -> {"aud":"infer-service","exp":ts,"sig":...}

# local client uses UDS and a tiny client lib that falls back to in-process cache
```

maya: sounds reasonable. Observability plan? we need per-tenant error rates, cache hit ratio, tail latency.

olivia: yes — dashboard + SLOs in RFC. Proposed metrics: tss.requests, tss.cache_hits, tss.cache_miss_latency, tss.sign_errors, per-tenant quota_denied. We'll gate rollout on error-rate <0.5% and cache-hit > 95% in staging.

samir: ops overhead — who owns the sidecar? infra team? or platform?

olivia: proposing Platform owns runbook and deployment; owning teams can opt-in for configuration. We'll add a Managed Mode for Dedicated customers where the sidecar runs in customer VPC as part of Private offering.

infra-bot: Created canary deployment: tss-canary/staging — helm chart v0.1.0 (olivia requested). Link: https://k8s.rw/canary/tss-canary

cheng: possible failure modes? cold-cache storms on rollout, signing key outage. How do we mitigate?

olivia: mitigations: 1) use exponential backoff + jitter for cold path; 2) circuit-breaker that falls back to conservative defaults (deny-safe or permissive depending on route policy); 3) short-lived assertions allow us to revoke quickly. We'll codify rollback playbooks.

maya: action items I can pick up: create the read-only flags spike, perf harness for UDS path, dashboard skeleton. olivia want me to file tickets?

olivia: please do — file: ARCH-ttss-1 (flags spike), ARCH-ttss-2 (perf harness), OBS-ttss-1 (dashboard). I'll add owners and timelines in RFC.

samir: +1 on spike. Also let's run a quick security review with sec-team before we move past read-only.

cheng: ack, will loop in sec. Also let's add a privacy checklist for no-PII guarantee.

olivia: thanks all. If no major objections I'll merge RFC in 48h and start the spike. Please react with :thumbsup: if you agree or leave comments on the doc.

maya: :thumbsup:

samir: :thumbsup:

olivia: leaving this thread open for any late feedback. Thanks!"
